title: Psycho Fox
subtitle: A fox with other forms to borrow
summary: Psycho Fox is Vic Tokai's platform game, first released for Master System in Europe in December 1989.
body: Psycho Fox is Vic Tokai's platform game, first released for Master System in Europe in December 1989. A young fox sets out to undo the damage caused by Madfox Daimyōjin, travelling through side-scrolling stages filled with enemies and alternative routes. A magical stick lets him transform into other animals, making the choice of body part of handling the landscape. The setting draws on fox-deity imagery, but its practical problem is immediate: reach the next stretch of ground with an animal whose abilities suit the obstacles waiting there.

The hippopotamus moves slowly and jumps poorly, but can break particular blocks. The monkey jumps higher, while the tiger runs faster. Switching forms therefore changes access as well as the feel of movement. A barrier that stops one animal may offer another a route onwards, giving the player a reason to inspect the stage before committing to a path. The transformations organise those differences around a small, readable set of strengths, so choosing an animal becomes a concrete response to a block, a gap or the space available for a run.

Bird Fly provides another useful companion. Carried with Psycho Fox, the bird can absorb a hit that would otherwise cost a life; thrown outward, it acts as a returning weapon. That dual use gives the player a reason to keep it close and another reason to send it towards an enemy. Fumito Tamayama and Hiroto Kanno composed the music. The animal forms and returning bird give the journey its identity, connecting an animated cast to the decisions made while crossing each stage's enemies, platforms and concealed routes.
